title: Find All Anagrams in a String
statement:
You are given two strings `s` and `p` made of lowercase English letters. An **anagram** of `p` is any string that uses exactly the same letters as `p`, each the same number of times, in any order.

Find every index `i` (0-indexed) such that the substring of `s` of length `|p|` starting at `i` is an anagram of `p`. Report the indices in increasing order. If `|p| > |s|` or no such index exists, report `-1`.

Overlapping matches all count.

**Follow-up:** Interviewers often ask how a frontend would consume this result (for example, highlighting every matching window in a text box), and then ask you to optimise time and space. Can you avoid re-sorting or re-counting each window from scratch?
input_format:
The first line contains the string `s`.
The second line contains the string `p`.
output_format: Print the matching start indices in increasing order, separated by single spaces, or `-1` if there are none.
constraints: `s` and `p` consist of lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The windows of length 3 are zyx, yxx, xxy, xyz, yzz, zzx, zxy. The windows at indices 0 (zyx), 3 (xyz) and 6 (zxy) contain one each of x, y and z.
Every window of length 2 is "aa", so the matches overlap at indices 0, 1 and 2.
`p` is longer than `s`, so no window can match.

hints: A window of fixed length |p| slides over `s`. Two strings are anagrams exactly when their letter counts are equal.
Do not recount each window. When the window moves one step right, add the new character's count and remove the one that left.
Track how many of the 26 letters currently have a matching count, so each step costs O(1) instead of comparing 26 counters.
brute:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
s, p = data[0], data[1]
res = []
for i in range(len(s) - len(p) + 1):
    if sorted(s[i:i + len(p)]) == sorted(p):
        res.append(i)
print(' '.join(map(str, res)) if res else -1)
